tasks.title: Read a column as text
tasks.statement: Read the id column as text and print its dtype.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO

df = pd.read_csv(StringIO("id\n007\n"), dtype={"id": str})
print(df["id"].dtype)

tasks.title: Write without the index

tasks.title: Inner join row count
tasks.statement: Merge the two frames on id with an inner join and print the row count.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "x": [10, 20]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "y": [30, 40]})
print(len(a.merge(b, on="id")))

tasks.title: Left join keeps every left row
tasks.statement: Left-join and print how many rows ended up without a match.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2], "y": [30]})
out = a.merge(b, on="id", how="left")
print(int(out["y"].isna().sum()))

tasks.title: Stack two frames
tasks.statement: Concatenate the frames vertically and print the resulting shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"x": [2]})
print(pd.concat([a, b], ignore_index=True).shape)

tasks.title: Count unmatched keys
tasks.statement: Use the merge indicator and print how many ids exist only on the left.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2]})
out = a.merge(b, on="id", how="left", indicator=True)
print(int((out["_merge"] == "left_only").sum()))

debug.title: A promised one-to-one that is not
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "x": [10]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1], "y": [20, 30]})
print(a.merge(b, on="id", validate="one_to_one").shape)
debug.fix:

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "x": [10]})

debug.title: A left join counted as the left rows
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 2], "y": [1, 2]})
print(len(a.merge(b, on="id", how="left")))
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 2], "y": [1, 2]})
print(len(a), len(a.merge(b, on="id", how="left")))
debug.error: Wrong output: 3 — the repeated right key multiplies the matched row, so the result is longer than the left table.

tasks.title: Sum per group
tasks.statement: Sum the values per city and print the mapping.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Pune", "Delhi"], "v": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.groupby("city")["v"].sum().to_dict())

tasks.title: Distance from the group mean
tasks.statement: Print how many rows are above their own group's mean.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a", "b", "b"], "v": [1, 3, 10, 20]})
print(int((df["v"] > df.groupby("g")["v"].transform("mean")).sum()))

tasks.title: Rows versus non-missing values
tasks.statement: Print the group size and the non-missing count for the single group.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a"], "v": [1.0, None]})
out = df.groupby("g").agg(n=("v", "size"), filled=("v", "count"))
print(out.values.tolist())

tasks.title: Named aggregation
tasks.statement: Produce total and average per group and print the column names.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a"], "v": [1]})
out = df.groupby("g").agg(total=("v", "sum"), average=("v", "mean"))
print(out.columns.tolist())

tasks.title: Pivot table shape
tasks.statement: Build a city × year table summed by value and print its shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Pune", "Delhi"], "year": [2025, 2026, 2026], "v": [1, 2, 3]})
t = df.pivot_table(index="city", columns="year", values="v", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
print(t.shape)
